import argparse
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter

from .parser import parse_lines


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="logparse", description="Summarize a simple log file.")
    ap.add_argument("path", help="log file to read")
    ap.add_argument("--level", help="only count lines at this level")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--json",
        action="store_true",
        help="print counts as a JSON object instead of a tab-separated table",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    with open(args.path) as f:
        lines = parse_lines(f)
    if args.level:
        lines = [l for l in lines if l.level == args.level]
    counts = Counter(l.level for l in lines)
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(dict(sorted(counts.items()))))
    else:
        for level, n in sorted(counts.items()):
            print(f"{level}\t{n}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import json

from logparse.cli import main


def test_json_flag_prints_counts_as_json_object(tmp_path, capsys):
    log = tmp_path / "app.log"
    log.write_text("INFO a\nERROR b\nINFO c\n")

    assert main(["--json", str(log)]) == 0

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert json.loads(out) == {"INFO": 2, "ERROR": 1}


def test_json_flag_respects_level_filter(tmp_path, capsys):
    log = tmp_path / "app.log"
    log.write_text("INFO a\nERROR b\nINFO c\n")

    assert main(["--json", "--level", "ERROR", str(log)]) == 0

    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out) == {"ERROR": 1}


def test_default_output_is_tab_separated_table(tmp_path, capsys):
    log = tmp_path / "app.log"
    log.write_text("INFO a\nERROR b\nINFO c\n")

    assert main([str(log)]) == 0

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == "ERROR\t1\nINFO\t2\n"

A tiny log-parsing CLI used as the scratch codebase for the Assignment 1 frontend demo.
Give Claude Code concrete tasks here ("find the bug that makes test_parse fail and fix it",
"add a --json flag and update the README") and watch the trajectory in the web UI.

## Usage

    python3 -m logparse.cli sample.log
    python3 -m logparse.cli --level ERROR sample.log
    python3 -m logparse.cli --json sample.log

By default the CLI prints one `LEVEL<TAB>count` line per level. Pass `--json` to
print the same counts as a single JSON object instead, e.g.
`{"DEBUG": 1, "ERROR": 1, "INFO": 2, "WARN": 1}`. `--json` can be combined with
`--level`.

## Tests

    python3 -m pytest -q

## Reset after a demo

    git checkout -- assignment1/demo-repo && git clean -fd assignment1/demo-repo

The project is a tiny Python package called `logparse` that parses log lines of the form `LEVEL message`, accepting only DEBUG, INFO, WARN, and ERROR and raising an error on any other level. Its command-line entry point reads a log file, optionally filters to one level, and prints per-level counts either as a tab-separated table or, with the `--json` flag, as a single sorted JSON object. The README describes it as a scratch codebase for the Assignment 1 frontend demo, with seven pytest tests covering parsing and CLI output and a five-line sample log to exercise them.
